task: Templates run inside with (locals), so anything an attacker manages to set on Object.prototype shows up as a template variable and can shadow EJS internals such as escapeFn, include and __append. Close this gadget. The source is lib/esm/ejs.js; lib/cjs is generated from it, so only edit the ESM file. By default the compiled template function must receive a shallow copy of the data in a null-prototype object, so the prototype chain of locals is not visible in the template. With Object.prototype.escapeFn set to a hijacking function, ejs.render("<%= name %>", { name: "<script>alert(1)</script>" }) must still return <script>alert(1)</script>. With Object.prototype.include polluted, <%- include("hello-world") %> must not call the polluted function, and with Object.prototype.__append polluted, ejs.render("<%= name %>", { name: "foo" }) must return foo without calling it. Add an opt-in boolean option, unsafePrototypeLocals, default false, that keeps the old behaviour: with function Data() {} and Data.prototype.greeting = "hi", ejs.render("<%= greeting %>", new Data(), { unsafePrototypeLocals: true }) returns hi. Setting Object.prototype.unsafePrototypeLocals = true must not turn the option on. A missing data argument must keep working.
accept: npx jake compile && node -e "const Mocha = require('mocha'); const m = new Mocha({ ui: 'tdd' }); m.addFile('test/ejs.js'); m.run((f) => { process.exitCode = f ? 1 : 0 })"
